subject: Re: MAP draft / POC environment dependencies (VPC peering, SSO, allowlists)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmemaps.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Jenna Lee <jenna.lee@acmemaps.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: MAP draft & POC env dependencies (post-call recap)

Hi Samir / Jenna 

Thanks again for the call today  great alignment on the POC goals and metrics. Per our discussion, I attached a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that breaks milestones, owners, and target dates. High-level POC goal: validate Redwood inference integration for Acme Maps tiling pipeline with target latency and cost thresholds.

Immediate MAP milestone I want to lock down: POC environment network & auth dependencies. From the call I captured the following items that we need to resolve to get your POC environment up and running:

- VPC peering / network connectivity: acme to redwood-managed VPC (or alternate: PrivateLink). Need target AWS account IDs, VPC CIDRs, and rough schedule for peering.
- IP allowlists / egress IPs: do you require our egress IP ranges, or will you provision NAT/egress IPs on your side?
- SSO / SAML: you mentioned Okta  please confirm SAML metadata XML or IdP URL, attribute mappings, and the SP entity metadata we should generate.
- Secrets/KMS: clarify whether Acme wants to manage secrets (AWS KMS) or have Redwood host encrypted secrets. If KMS, we'll need IAM cross-account role or key policy details.

Proposed target for completing the network/auth milestone: 2026-06-12 (aligned with POC kickoff). If that date is aggressive, tell me what works and we'll update the MAP.

Next steps / asks for this week:
1) Please confirm POC target date (we suggested 2026-06-12).
2) Share the AWS account ID(s) + VPC CIDR(s) we should expect to peer with (or confirm preference for PrivateLink).
3) Provide Okta SAML metadata and the name/email attribute you expect.
4) Indicate preference for secrets: Acme-managed KMS (cross-account) vs Redwood-managed KMS.

I've attached the MAP draft (20260512-acme-map-map-draft.xlsx) as a starting point. Nikhil from our SE team is looped in to help with technical specifics once you share the details.

Thanks  happy to hop on a short call this week to walk through the MAP.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft & POC env dependencies (post-call recap)

Thanks Marissa  good summary, and Jenna and I reviewed the MAP draft. Quick answers below; added a couple questions inline.

- POC target date: We can target a POC kickoff week of 2026-06-08 with a completion goal of 2026-06-30. If you need full infra healthy by the 8th, we'll prioritize the network tasks.
- AWS accounts / VPCs: Primary AWS account: 111122223333, VPC CIDR: 10.10.0.0/16. We'll be able to create a peering connection during the week of 5/25.
- IP allowlists: We'll host the POC in our VPC; prefer to add Redwood egress IPs to our allowlist. Can you share your egress IP ranges or advise if you prefer peering only?
- SSO / SAML: We run Okta. I'll pull the SAML metadata and send it by EOD Thursday. Attribute mapping: email --> email, name --> name.
- Secrets/KMS: We prefer Acme-managed KMS. We can create a CMK and add a key policy that allows a cross-account role.

Questions from our side:
1) For peering, do you require route table changes or a proxy? Any inbound ports we need to open beyond 443?
2) If we provide a KMS key policy, what IAM role/ARN should we whitelist?

Attaching a network diagram that shows the expected peering / route flows.

Samir
Senior Infrastructure Manager | Acme Maps
samir.patel@acmemaps.com
+1 (650) 555-0133

Attachment: network-diagram-acme.pdf (pdf, 86KB)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acmemaps.com>
Cc: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>, Jenna Lee <jenna.lee@acmemaps.com>
Date: Wed, 13 May 2026 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft & POC env dependencies (post-call recap)

Perfect  appreciate the quick responses and the diagram. Inline replies below and an updated short MAP view:

Inline answers:
- Peering / routing: For a standard VPC peering setup we'll need you to accept the peering request and add a route pointing the Redwood VPC CIDR to the peering connection. On our side, we will also add routes to send inference traffic into your VPC. No inbound ports beyond 443 are required for production traffic; we sometimes ask for SSH (22) into a bastion for debugging but that can be short-lived and locked to specific admin IPs.
- Egress IPs: We'll provide a recommended egress IP range (we can pin a small pool in front of the service)  that will let you add an allowlist entry instead of peering if you prefer.
- KMS/IAM: If you create a CMK and add a key policy, we'll need an IAM role ARN that Redwood can assume. I'll have Nikhil follow up with the exact role ARN we expect.

Updated MAP excerpt (milestones / owners / target date):
- Milestone: Provide SAML metadata + confirm attribute mapping  Owner: Acme (Jenna)  Target: 2026-05-20
- Milestone: Provide AWS account ID + VPC CIDR + accept peering request  Owner: Acme (Samir)  Target: 2026-05-25
- Milestone: Redwood provides egress IP ranges & peering request  Owner: Redwood (Marissa / Nikhil)  Target: 2026-05-22
- Milestone: KMS cross-account access configured  Owner: Acme (Samir) / Redwood (Nikhil)  Target: 2026-05-28
- Milestone: POC infra smoke test (connectivity & auth)  Owner: Redwood / Acme SRE  Target: 2026-06-03

I'll attach an updated MAP spreadsheet after Nikhil confirms the role ARN. Does that plan work for you? If so we'll lock the MAP and schedule a 30-min runbook call for the 5/26 week to walk through peering steps.

Thanks  Marissa

Attachment: 20260513-acme-map-map-draft.xlsx (xlsx, 44KB)
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP draft & POC env dependencies (technical follow-up)

Hi Samir  quick technical notes / checklist from our SE side so the peering and KMS steps go smoothly:

1) Redwood VPC CIDR: 10.20.0.0/16 (we'll include exact AZ subnets in the peering request).
2) Peering flow: We'll initiate the peering request from our account (222233334444). Once accepted, please add the route table entry that sends 10.20.0.0/16 to the peering connection.
3) Security groups / ports: For the inference endpoint we only need 443 inbound from your VPC. For debugging we may request ephemeral SSH to a bastion  we will coordinate exact admin IPs when necessary.
4) Egress IPs: If you prefer allowlisting IPs, we'll provide a pool (example: 34.213.90.0/27)  final ranges to be confirmed.
5) KMS / IAM: Preferred pattern: Acme creates a CMK and a role ARN that Redwood can assume (sts:AssumeRole). Please include the role ARN in the key policy. We will need the role ARN format: arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/RedwoodPOCKeyAccess. If you prefer an alternate name, tell us and we'll adjust.

If helpful, I'm happy to join your infra call to walk SREs through the peering accept and route table steps.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwoodinference.com

All  thanks for the clarity. The plan looks good and we'll proceed on the timeline below:

Action items we committed to this week:
- 5/14 5/18: Jenna to pull Okta SAML metadata and send to Marissa. (Owner: Jenna)
- By 5/25: Samir to accept peering request and confirm route table changes (Owner: Samir)
- By 5/22: Redwood to send egress IP ranges and initiate peering request (Owner: Marissa / Nikhil)
- By 5/28: Acme to add KMS key policy with role arn:aws:iam::111122223333:role/RedwoodPOCKeyAccess (Owner: Samir)

POC kickoff target: week of 2026-06-08 (we'll aim for infra smoke test by 2026-06-03 per the MAP). If anything slips we'll update the MAP and communicate changes in HubSpot.

I'll upload the Okta metadata now and ping when it's in. Thanks everyone  looking forward to getting started.

Samir
